question.problem: Given that $X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7)$ and $Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.6)$ are independent, calculate $P(X=1 \, \cap \, Y=1).$
question.worked_solution:
Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=1) & =P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=1).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7),$ we have

$$
P(X=1) = 0.7, \quad P(X=0) = 0.3,
$$

and since $Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.6),$ we have

$$
P(Y=1)=0.6, \quad P(Y=0)=0.4.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=1) & =P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=1) \\  & =0.7\cdot 0.6 \\  & =0.42.\end{aligned}
$$
